contract.cleanup: Open all callback and milestone gates. Initiate readable cancellation and writable abortion on still-live owners before joining, so missing HWM0 demand cannot strand an in-flight write. Join original API/closed/ready promises and dynamically recorded callback results, then release owners and observe post-release promises. Require zero pending work, timers and public locks; separate owned-process teardown remains mandatory.
contract.distinctness: Weighted writable queue accounting drives ready-promise identity and threshold transitions, independently from individual write completion.

t.equal(writer.desiredSize, 1, 'in-flight two-byte write retains its weight');
t.same(writer.ready, ready0, 'below-pressure admission retains original ready promise');
t.equal(writer.desiredSize, 0, 'two plus one bytes fill weighted capacity');
t.equal(ready1 === ready0, false, 'threshold crossing allocates a new ready epoch');

t.equal(writer.desiredSize, 2, 'first completion restores two units with second still in flight');
t.equal(b.status, 'pending', 'ready fulfillment does not require held second write to finish');

t.equal(writer.desiredSize, 3, 'full drain restores initial weighted capacity');

t.equal(writer.desiredSize, 3, 'final completion restores capacity');

intended_oracle: desiredSize is 3 initially, 1 after first admission, 0 after second, 2 with only second in flight, 3 after drain, 0 after final 3-byte admission, and 0 after closed.
Below-threshold ready is the original fulfilled promise; at pressure it is a new pending promise, reused while pressure remains; a later threshold crossing allocates a different epoch.
The pressure ready resolves before the held second write resolves, proving readiness is capacity rather than total queue emptiness.
FIFO sink trace, maxActive=1, exact fixed byte arrays, one close, no abort, joined promises and released writer lock are scaffolding, not additional credit.
